name: Arker

modes.label: AWS US VMs, on-demand run time (docs planning-table rates)
modes.note: hour = 'Arker AWS US, 1 month' planning-table cost / 1,000 VMs / 730 h ($137,047 small, $271,572 large). The live rate card is behind login (arker.ai/console/pricing); these are the only public Arker numbers. Arker says it bills 'run time, not machine time': VMs scale to zero between runs and can be suspended by policy while waiting on outbound (e.g. LLM) responses, so use the run_time_pct knob. Only two presets are priced publicly although VMs are resizable (up to 32 vCPU / 64 GiB in the catalog).

modes.label: AWS US pool, 12-month commitment (always-on, 19.55% off)
modes.commit_note: Pools = reserved bare-metal capacity bought for a term (min 30 days), billed on the next invoice whether used or not; cannot be deleted. Private access for partnered companies. Per-instance month = planning table 12-month row / 1,000 (small $110.259, large $218.488; month_cap per size).

modes.label: AWS US pool, 24-month commitment (always-on, 22.83% off)
modes.commit_note: As commit-12m; 24-month row. AWS has no 2-year Savings Plan, so Arker backs this with a 'procurement ladder'.

modes.label: Proposed Arker EU on Hetzner, 1-month (not a published offer)
modes.commit_note: Commit discounts 3% / 5% / 7.69% at 12/24/36 months (36-month: $20,376 / $47,591 per 1,000 VMs).
modes.note: NEVER PRICED (flag legacy = not on sale): docs 2026-09-28 still say "Arker EU rows are proposed prices, not currently published offers." Docs: 'Arker EU rows are proposed prices, not currently published offers.' $22,074 / $51,556 per 1,000 VMs per month (730 h). Priced ~30% over amortized AX42 host cost.

modes.label: Proposed Arker EU on Scaleway, 1-month (not a published offer)
modes.commit_note: Commit discounts 10% / 20% / 30% at 12/24/36 months (36-month: $15,822 / $31,644 per 1,000 VMs).
modes.note: NEVER PRICED (flag legacy = not on sale): docs 2026-09-28 still say "Arker EU rows are proposed prices, not currently published offers." Proposed, not offered. $22,603 / $45,205 per 1,000 VMs per month (730 h). Markup ~50% on-demand falling to ~24% at 36 months.

plans.name: Paid account (pay as you go)
plans.note: No subscription fee is mentioned anywhere public; the price catalog is behind login. No free tier ('we don't currently offer a free tier').

plans.name: Private region / VPC / on-prem, private networking, pools
plans.note: Contact support@arker.ai. Pools in private access for partnered background-agent companies.

features.ip_note: VMs run in AWS regions (e.g. aws-us-west-2), so egress is cloud datacenter IPs; no proxy/residential options documented.

perf_source: benchmarks.json providers.arker.computesdk: cold_start_tti median 75.56 ms (2026-08-07, 1 run), burst_tti median 254.2 ms at 100 concurrency (2026-09-25), dax 60.53 s (2026-09-25; sandbox reported 8 vCPU / 15.84 GiB aarch64, i.e. Graviton). No hpc CPU run.

knobs.label: Share of session the VM is actually running (not scaled to zero / suspended)
knobs.why: Arker says it charges for run time, not machine time: VMs scale to zero between runs and a scaling policy can suspend a VM while it waits on outbound (LLM) responses or between inbound requests. The exact metering rule is not public, so default is 1 (billed like wall-clock).

caveats: No public list rate card: arker.ai/pricing redirects to arker.ai/console/pricing behind a WorkOS login. All on-demand/commit prices are derived from the docs 'Replicas capacity planning' table (1,000 always-on VMs x 730 h), which may be illustrative rather than live offers.
Only two public shapes (small 2/8/32, large 4/16/32). A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB workload is priced on the large preset ($0.372/h) because nothing public prices 4/8.

Derived (fragile) unit rates: solving small, large and the pools-doc example quote (aws us-west, 32 vCPU / 64 GiB / 256 GiB for 30 days = $1,428) gives ~$0.0301/vCPU-h, ~$0.0155/GiB-h RAM, ~$0.000108/GiB-h disk (~4/8 = $0.244/h). Not used in modes.

'Charges for run time, not machine time' is marketing text; whether idle/suspended VMs pay for memory/disk retention is not published (paused_ram_billed null). Prices exclude persistent storage; filesystem (object-storage volume) price unpublished.
Commit modes are pools: private access, minimum 30-day term, prepaid on the next invoice, cannot be deleted; after expiry VMs keep running at normal rates. Modeled as always-on per-instance.
EU Hetzner/Scaleway rows are explicitly "proposed prices, not currently published offers" (re-checked 2026-09-28): flagged legacy so they are never priced.
Egress, IPv4 and GPU prices are not published (GPU types exist in arker us-west and gcp us-central1; fractional vGPU from 0.125).
No free tier. Billing granularity and minimums unknown.

unverified: may bill run time only (active). Docs: "charge for run time, not machine time" (https://arker.ai/docs/pricing); the metering rule (what counts as run time, suspended-VM memory/disk) is unpublished, so modes keep alloc and the run_time_pct knob approximates it.

Snapshot / persistent-storage price not published ("Prices exclude persistent storage and taxes", docs/pricing, 2026-09-28): snapshot_gib_month stays null, so retained state shows as unknown, not free.

nested_virt is opt-in and placement-limited: fork API `nestedvirt` = "Give an `image` or `dockerfile` VM access to `/dev/kvm`. Unsupported placements return `400`." (arker.ai/docs/api/fork.md, checked 2026-09-28). Which placements support it and any price difference are not published.

snapshot_auto.quote: Every VM's memory and disk are persistent by default on local NVMe and on remote object storage when idle.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: VM goes idle (no active run) or a scaling policy suspends it (e.g. while waiting on an outbound LLM response); resumes automatically on next run / inbound request. Memory (running processes) included. Intro also says Arker can 'transparently snapshot machines at high frequency and restore to other hosts in the event of failure' (https://arker.ai/docs.md) and 'durable' VMs make every run a transaction.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Omit it or pass `["disk", "memory"]` for a warm fork that resumes the source filesystem and running processes.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No separate named-snapshot endpoint: the checkpoint primitive is POST /v1/fork of any of your VMs (source_vm_id), which copies disk + memory into a new VM that can itself be forked again (template), or disk-only with layers ['disk']. Memory included; new machines boot from it. Can be marked public for other orgs. No explicit 'restore in place' to an earlier point.

harness_api.quote: The Arker API is a small set of operations over machines and filesystems.
harness_api.note: Full operation list = fork, vms, policies, runs (generic command exec with durable runs, sessions, PTY), sync, mounts, filesystems. Agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Aider) are only preinstalled in the ubuntu-coding public VM ('sign in with your own credentials'), no agent-level prompt/stream/resume API.

egress_allowlist.quote: With a non-empty rule list, unmatched outbound traffic is denied.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-VM policy document (PUT /v1/vms/{id}/policies), first-match rules on hosts (SNI/Host suffix match), IPs/CIDRs and ports; 'Layer-4 rules (ips/ports/hosts) are enforced in kernel' on the host side. Deny-all egress with a single rule. Added July 2026.

egress_http_rules.quote: layer-7 criteria and the `rewrite`/`gate`/`scaling` actions run through a managed proxy.
egress_http_rules.note: L7 match on methods, paths (segment prefix), headers, body_contains; actions allow/deny/rewrite (host, path, headers, body)/gate (external HTTP authorization call per request, fail-closed by default).

ingress_rules.quote: Only ports in an explicit inbound allow rule are exposed.
ingress_rules.note: Inbound rules pick exposed ports, auth 'arker' (Bearer API key of the owning org, default) or 'open' (public); match on caller source IPs/CIDRs. URL form <vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM (custom hypervisor) with root and systemd; not stated in docs.

secret_proxy.quote: Keep an Anthropic API key out of the machine: match calls to `api.anthropic.com` and set the key from a rewrite. Code in the machine calls Anthropic with no credentials; the proxy injects it.
secret_proxy.note: Outbound rewrite rules work on any host match and can set headers, path, host or body with ${secret:NAME} named secrets (encrypted at rest, redacted on read). HTTP(S) only via the managed L7 proxy; no mention of databases/SSH/git-over-SSH.

volume_attach.quote: A filesystem is a standalone, persistent, network-attached, object-storage-backed volume that outlives any single machine.
volume_attach.note: POST /v1/filesystems then POST /v1/vms/{id}/mounts at a path. Price unpublished.

volume_shared.quote: so one filesystem can be mounted into many machines. Reads and writes under the path land in the shared volume.
volume_shared.note: read-write, object-storage-backed network filesystem; consistency semantics not documented.
